title: Few-shot Adaptation Works with UnpredicTable Data
date_source: page byline ("August 7, 2022"); cited arXiv eprint 2208.01009, year 2022
rule_cited: §2 — FAR.AI-asserted, evidence-backed measured result, independently codeable
reason: KEYWORD-FILTER FALSE NEGATIVE: a title with no evaluation vocabulary ('UnpredicTable Data') hides a quantified few-shot-learning measurement over 52 downstream tasks. Full abstract with numbers is on the landing page, so the finding is evidence-backed in this report.

findings.finding: Finetuning language models on a single narrow subset of 413,299 automatically-extracted internet-table tasks (software documentation tables) raised mean few-shot-learning performance by +7.5% across 52 downstream NLP tasks, beating finetuning on 40 human-curated NLP datasets (+6.7%); FSL gains did not scale proportionally with dataset size and narrow subsets sometimes beat more diverse ones.
findings.finding_quote: raises FSL performance by a mean of +7.5% on 52 downstream tasks; which beats training on 40 human-curated NLP datasets (+6.7%)
findings.models_systems: Language models finetuned on the UnpredicTable dataset (no specific model named on the landing page)
findings.tier_reasoning: Gate 1 yes — a measured empirical result on finetuned language models. Gate 2 fails (b) and (c): no specific company or model is named on this page, and the result is a positive capability/data-composition finding with no dangerous threshold crossed, so no company response is reasonable.

title: Training Language Models with Language Feedback
date_source: page byline ("November 16, 2022"); citation year 2022
rule_cited: §2 — FAR.AI-asserted, two evidence-backed measured results, independently codeable
reason: KEYWORD-FILTER FALSE NEGATIVE: a training-method title conceals two measured results, one of which is an explicit capability threshold ('only large language models (175B parameters) do so') and one a named-model result on GPT-3.

findings.finding: In synthetic experiments, only language models at the 175B-parameter scale accurately incorporated natural-language feedback to produce refinements of their own outputs; smaller models did not.
findings.finding_quote: finding that only large language models (175B parameters) do so
findings.models_systems: Language models of varying scale up to 175B parameters (GPT-3 family)
findings.domain: alignment training methodology / emergent capability threshold
findings.tier_reasoning: Gate 1 yes — a measured empirical result about model behaviour at different scales. Gate 2 fails (c): a scale threshold for a beneficial capability is not a concerning result for which a company response is reasonable; §4 also excludes capability trends.

findings.finding: A three-step learning algorithm using only 100 samples of human-written natural-language feedback finetuned a GPT-3 model to roughly human-level summarization ability, indicating language feedback is far more sample-efficient per human evaluation than pairwise comparison feedback.
findings.finding_quote: Using only 100 samples of human-written feedback, our learning algorithm finetunes a GPT-3 model to roughly human-level summarization ability.
findings.domain: alignment training methodology / human feedback sample efficiency
findings.tier_reasoning: Gate 1 yes — a measured empirical result on a named model. Gate 2 names a company/model (b satisfied) but fails (c): the result is a positive alignment-method result on GPT-3 with no dangerous threshold crossed, and GPT-3 is used as the instrument of a methodology study.
